correctness.rationale: Proposition 5.2 of arXiv:2609.36313v2 reduces any finite-dimensional interpretation of \(\omega,<\) to dimension one while preserving order type \(\omega\). Fix the finite parameter tuple \(A\) used by that interpretation. Each quotient level \(L_n\) is \(A\)-definable because the \(n\)-th point of \(\omega,<\) is first-order definable. The levels are pairwise disjoint and nonempty. In a minimal structure an infinite definable level would be cofinite, leaving only finitely many points for all other levels, impossible. Thus every \(L_n\) is finite, so every element of \(M\) belongs to a finite \(A\)-definable set and hence to \(\operatorname{acl}(A)\). The locally finite algebraic-closure corollary is immediate.

value.rationale: The conclusion turns a recent dimension-reduction theorem into an algebraic obstruction that can be checked without constructing or classifying definable orders. In particular, any minimal structure with locally finite algebraic closure is immediately excluded from finite-dimensional interpretations of \(\omega,<\). This is a structural criterion directly relevant to the interpretability questions motivating the source, rather than a notation change or a finite recomputation.
